t: You're looking at a standing bronze statue of Winston Churchill, in the Members' Lobby of the House of Commons. He is shown mid-stride, with his hands on his hips. The sculptor was Oscar Nemon, born in Osijek in Croatia, who settled in England and is best known for a series of more than a dozen public statues of Churchill. The setting suits the subject. Churchill was an MP for some sixty-two years between 1900 and 1964, and Prime Minister from 1940 to 1945 and again from 1951 to 1955.
